title: Five Lyft fee offsets under review after revised wheelchair pickup times

beats.text: Lyft says five fee offsets in Los Angeles no longer qualify. This is an investigative lead.

visual.sub: Lyft revised its assessment of eligibility for previously approved fee offsets

beats.text: The state had approved about $4.63 million for those quarters.

visual.kicker: Lyft revised its assessment of eligibility for previously approved fee offsets

beats.text: In February 2026, Lyft initially said its corrected times left eligibility unchanged.

visual.kicker: The first attempted correction said no quarter’s eligibility changed

beats.text: In June, after consulting state staff, it withdrew both early filings.

visual.kicker: The first attempted correction said no quarter’s eligibility changed

beats.text: We matched the five amounts to five separate approval certificates.
The first covered about $945,267 for the final quarter of 2023.

visual.heading: Los Angeles approvals
visual.context: Two later quarters and all five combined

beats.text: In that quarter, Los Angeles originally reported 74.42 percent within the first time standard.

visual.kicker: One Los Angeles quarter moved from above to just below its governing threshold

beats.text: The corrected share was 70.94 percent. It needed 71 percent.
Lyft marked every San Francisco quarter unaffected.
The regulator listed further review through January 2027.

visual.kicker: The public record separates the San Francisco result from the pending Los Angeles review

beats.text: A final ruling and a payment record would show if any money returned.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
